attributionText: DecisionEats original meal-template variation. Materialized from explicit ingredients and cooking components; not an independently sourced or individually kitchen-tested recipe.
instructions:
Makes 2 servings. Use plain, unseasoned protein and vegetables. Wash produce and measure the ingredients. Cut broccoli into small florets and carrots into thin half-moons.

Bring 200 ml water to a boil in a saucepan. Remove from the heat, stir in the dry instant couscous, cover and stand for 5 minutes. Fluff; use standard instant couscous, not pearl couscous. Cook the skillet mixture while the base cooks.

Drain and rinse the canned black beans. These must be canned, ready-to-eat beans, not dried beans. Heat half the olive oil in a large skillet. Stir the beans over medium heat for 5 minutes, then transfer to a plate.

Add the remaining olive oil to the skillet. Add the prepared vegetables (holding back any spinach), stir for 2 minutes, then add 60 ml water. Cover and cook over medium heat for 8-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the firmest vegetables are tender. Add any reserved spinach for the final 3 minutes. Uncover and let excess water evaporate.

Peel and finely grate the ginger. Stir it, the cumin and turmeric into the tender vegetables for 1 minute. Add coconut milk and simmer for 4 minutes, then stir in the lime juice.

Return the cooked protein to the skillet. Stir gently and heat for 3-5 minutes until piping hot throughout. If too thick, add water a tablespoon at a time. Divide the cooked base and skillet mixture between two bowls and serve promptly. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and reheat until piping hot throughout.

instructions:
Makes 2 servings. Use plain, unseasoned protein and vegetables. Wash produce and measure the ingredients. Cut zucchini into thin half-moons and slice the mushrooms.

Rinse the dry long-grain white rice. Bring it and 320 ml water to a boil in a saucepan. Cover, reduce to low and cook for 15-20 minutes until tender and the water is absorbed. Rest covered for 5 minutes; fluff. Cook the skillet mixture while the base cooks.

Drain and rinse the canned black beans. These must be canned, ready-to-eat beans, not dried beans. Heat half the olive oil in a large skillet. Stir the beans over medium heat for 5 minutes, then transfer to a plate.

Add the remaining olive oil to the skillet. Add the prepared vegetables (holding back any spinach), stir for 2 minutes, then add 60 ml water. Cover and cook over medium heat for 8-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the firmest vegetables are tender. Add any reserved spinach for the final 3 minutes. Uncover and let excess water evaporate.

Peel and finely grate the ginger; finely chop the garlic. Stir both into the tender vegetables for 1 minute. Add soy sauce, rice vinegar and 60 ml water, then simmer for 2 minutes.

Return the cooked protein to the skillet. Stir gently and heat for 3-5 minutes until piping hot throughout. If too thick, add water a tablespoon at a time. Divide the cooked base and skillet mixture between two bowls and serve promptly. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and reheat until piping hot throughout.

Makes 2 servings. Use plain, unseasoned protein and vegetables. Wash produce and measure the ingredients. Slice the zucchini thinly. Remove pepper seeds and cut into thin strips.

Bring 1.5 liters water to a boil in a saucepan. Add plain dry rice noodles and cook for 3-8 minutes, following their packet time, until tender. Drain and rinse briefly with warm water to prevent sticking. Cook the skillet mixture while the base cooks.

Drain and rinse the canned black beans. These must be canned, ready-to-eat beans, not dried beans. Heat half the olive oil in a large skillet. Stir the beans over medium heat for 5 minutes, then transfer to a plate.

Add the remaining olive oil to the skillet. Add the prepared vegetables (holding back any spinach), stir for 2 minutes, then add 60 ml water. Cover and cook over medium heat for 8-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the firmest vegetables are tender. Add any reserved spinach for the final 3 minutes. Uncover and let excess water evaporate.

Peel and finely grate the ginger. Whisk it with smooth peanut butter, lime juice, soy sauce and 90 ml warm water. Pour into the tender vegetables and simmer gently for 3 minutes, stirring.

Return the cooked protein to the skillet. Stir gently and heat for 3-5 minutes until piping hot throughout. If too thick, add water a tablespoon at a time. Divide the cooked base and skillet mixture between two bowls and serve promptly. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and reheat until piping hot throughout.

Return the cooked protein to the skillet. Stir gently and heat for 3-5 minutes until piping hot throughout. If too thick, add water a tablespoon at a time. Divide the cooked base and skillet mixture between two bowls and serve promptly. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and reheat until piping hot throughout.

Add the remaining olive oil to the skillet. Add the prepared vegetables (holding back any spinach), stir for 2 minutes, then add 60 ml water. Peel and finely grate the ginger; finely chop the garlic. Stir both into the tender vegetables for 1 minute. Add soy sauce, rice vinegar and 60 ml water, then simmer for 2 minutes.

Return the cooked protein to the skillet. Stir gently and heat for 3-5 minutes until piping hot throughout. If too thick, add water a tablespoon at a time. Divide the cooked base and skillet mixture between two bowls and serve promptly. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and reheat until piping hot throughout.

Makes 2 servings. Use plain, unseasoned protein and vegetables. Wash produce and measure the ingredients. Remove pepper seeds and slice thinly. Keep the frozen corn ready.

Rinse the dry long-grain white rice. Bring it and 320 ml water to a boil in a saucepan. Cover, reduce to low and cook for 15-20 minutes until tender and the water is absorbed. Rest covered for 5 minutes; fluff. Cook the skillet mixture while the base cooks.

Cut the boneless chicken breast into 2 cm pieces on a separate board. Heat half the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken for 8-12 minutes, stirring, until every piece reaches 165 F (74 C) in the center. Transfer to a clean plate; wash hands and utensils.

Add the remaining olive oil to the skillet. Add the prepared vegetables (holding back any spinach), stir for 2 minutes, then add 60 ml water. Cover and cook over medium heat for 8-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the firmest vegetables are tender. Add any reserved spinach for the final 3 minutes. Uncover and let excess water evaporate.

Peel and finely grate the ginger; finely chop the garlic. Stir both into the tender vegetables for 1 minute. Add soy sauce, rice vinegar and 60 ml water, then simmer for 2 minutes.

Return the cooked protein to the skillet. Stir gently and heat for 3-5 minutes until piping hot throughout. If too thick, add water a tablespoon at a time. Divide the cooked base and skillet mixture between two bowls and serve promptly. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and reheat until piping hot throughout.

Divide the cooked base and skillet mixture between two bowls and serve promptly. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and reheat until piping hot throughout.

Makes 2 servings. Use plain, unseasoned protein and vegetables. Wash produce and measure the ingredients. Remove tough kale stems and finely slice the leaves. Chop the tomatoes.

Rinse the dry quinoa well. Bring it and 360 ml water to a boil in a saucepan. Cover and simmer gently for 15-20 minutes until tender. Rest off the heat for 5 minutes and fluff. Cook the skillet mixture while the base cooks.

Cut the boneless chicken breast into 2 cm pieces on a separate board. Heat half the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken for 8-12 minutes, stirring, until every piece reaches 165 F (74 C) in the center. Transfer to a clean plate; wash hands and utensils.

Add the remaining olive oil to the skillet. Add the prepared vegetables (holding back any spinach), stir for 2 minutes, then add 60 ml water. Cover and cook over medium heat for 8-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the firmest vegetables are tender. Add any reserved spinach for the final 3 minutes. Uncover and let excess water evaporate.

Finely chop the garlic and stir it into the tender vegetables for 1 minute. Add the canned tomatoes and basil; break up the tomatoes and simmer 5 minutes.

Return the cooked protein to the skillet. Stir gently and heat for 3-5 minutes until piping hot throughout. If too thick, add water a tablespoon at a time. Divide the cooked base and skillet mixture between two bowls and serve promptly. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and reheat until piping hot throughout.

Makes 2 servings. Use plain, unseasoned protein and vegetables. Wash produce and measure the ingredients. Slice the mushrooms and keep the frozen peas ready.

Rinse the dry quinoa well. Bring it and 360 ml water to a boil in a saucepan. Cover and simmer gently for 15-20 minutes until tender. Rest off the heat for 5 minutes and fluff. Cook the skillet mixture while the base cooks.

Cut the boneless chicken breast into 2 cm pieces on a separate board. Heat half the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken for 8-12 minutes, stirring, until every piece reaches 165 F (74 C) in the center. Transfer to a clean plate; wash hands and utensils.

Add the remaining olive oil to the skillet. Add the prepared vegetables (holding back any spinach), stir for 2 minutes, then add 60 ml water. Cover and cook over medium heat for 8-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the firmest vegetables are tender. Add any reserved spinach for the final 3 minutes. Uncover and let excess water evaporate.

Peel and finely grate the ginger. Whisk it with smooth peanut butter, lime juice, soy sauce and 90 ml warm water. Pour into the tender vegetables and simmer gently for 3 minutes, stirring.

Return the cooked protein to the skillet. Stir gently and heat for 3-5 minutes until piping hot throughout. If too thick, add water a tablespoon at a time. Divide the cooked base and skillet mixture between two bowls and serve promptly. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and reheat until piping hot throughout.

Makes 2 servings. Use plain, unseasoned protein and vegetables. Wash produce and measure the ingredients. Remove pepper seeds and slice the pepper and onion thinly.

Rinse the dry quinoa well. Bring it and 360 ml water to a boil in a saucepan. Cover and simmer gently for 15-20 minutes until tender. Rest off the heat for 5 minutes and fluff. Cook the skillet mixture while the base cooks.

Cut the boneless chicken breast into 2 cm pieces on a separate board. Heat half the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken for 8-12 minutes, stirring, until every piece reaches 165 F (74 C) in the center. Transfer to a clean plate; wash hands and utensils.

Add the remaining olive oil to the skillet. Add the prepared vegetables (holding back any spinach), stir for 2 minutes, then add 60 ml water. Cover and cook over medium heat for 8-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the firmest vegetables are tender. Add any reserved spinach for the final 3 minutes. Uncover and let excess water evaporate.

Peel and finely grate the ginger; finely chop the garlic. Stir both into the tender vegetables for 1 minute. Add soy sauce, rice vinegar and 60 ml water, then simmer for 2 minutes.

Return the cooked protein to the skillet. Stir gently and heat for 3-5 minutes until piping hot throughout. If too thick, add water a tablespoon at a time. Divide the cooked base and skillet mixture between two bowls and serve promptly. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and reheat until piping hot throughout.

Divide the cooked base and skillet mixture between two bowls and serve promptly. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and reheat until piping hot throughout.

Divide the cooked base and skillet mixture between two bowls and serve promptly. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and reheat until piping hot throughout.

Makes 2 servings. Use plain, unseasoned protein and vegetables. Wash produce and measure the ingredients. Chop the tomatoes; wash and roughly chop the spinach. Reserve the spinach for the final 3 minutes of vegetable cooking.

Bring 200 ml water to a boil in a saucepan. Remove from the heat, stir in the dry instant couscous, cover and stand for 5 minutes. Fluff; use standard instant couscous, not pearl couscous. Cook the skillet mixture while the base cooks.

Drain and rinse the canned chickpeas. These must be canned, ready-to-eat beans, not dried beans. Heat half the olive oil in a large skillet. Stir the chickpeas over medium heat for 5 minutes, then transfer to a plate.

Add the remaining olive oil to the skillet. Add the prepared vegetables (holding back any spinach), stir for 2 minutes, then add 60 ml water. Cover and cook over medium heat for 8-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the firmest vegetables are tender. Add any reserved spinach for the final 3 minutes. Uncover and let excess water evaporate.

Stir paprika, cumin and tomato paste into the tender vegetables for 1 minute. Add the lemon juice and 90 ml water; stir and simmer for 3 minutes.

Return the cooked protein to the skillet. Stir gently and heat for 3-5 minutes until piping hot throughout. If too thick, add water a tablespoon at a time. Divide the cooked base and skillet mixture between two bowls and serve promptly. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and reheat until piping hot throughout.

Makes 2 servings. Use plain, unseasoned protein and vegetables. Wash produce and measure the ingredients. Cut broccoli into small florets and carrots into thin half-moons.

Bring 1.5 liters water to a boil in a saucepan. Add dry wheat pasta and boil for 10-12 minutes, or the packet time, until tender. Drain. Cook the skillet mixture while the base cooks.

Drain plain firm tofu, pat it dry and cut into 2 cm cubes. Heat half the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the tofu for 8-10 minutes, turning gently, until golden. Transfer to a clean plate.

Add the remaining olive oil to the skillet. Add the prepared vegetables (holding back any spinach), stir for 2 minutes, then add 60 ml water. Cover and cook over medium heat for 8-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the firmest vegetables are tender. Add any reserved spinach for the final 3 minutes. Uncover and let excess water evaporate.

Finely chop the garlic. Stir it and the oregano into the tender vegetables for 1 minute. Stir in the lemon juice and 60 ml water.

Return the cooked protein to the skillet. Stir gently and heat for 3-5 minutes until piping hot throughout. If too thick, add water a tablespoon at a time. Divide the cooked base and skillet mixture between two bowls and serve promptly. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and reheat until piping hot throughout.

Makes 2 servings. Use plain, unseasoned protein and vegetables. Wash produce and measure the ingredients. Slice the mushrooms and keep the frozen peas ready.

Bring 200 ml water to a boil in a saucepan. Remove from the heat, stir in the dry instant couscous, cover and stand for 5 minutes. Fluff; use standard instant couscous, not pearl couscous. Cook the skillet mixture while the base cooks.

Drain plain firm tofu, pat it dry and cut into 2 cm cubes. Heat half the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the tofu for 8-10 minutes, turning gently, until golden. Transfer to a clean plate.

Add the remaining olive oil to the skillet. Add the prepared vegetables (holding back any spinach), stir for 2 minutes, then add 60 ml water. Cover and cook over medium heat for 8-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the firmest vegetables are tender. Add any reserved spinach for the final 3 minutes. Uncover and let excess water evaporate.

Peel and finely grate the ginger; finely chop the garlic. Stir both into the tender vegetables for 1 minute. Add soy sauce, rice vinegar and 60 ml water, then simmer for 2 minutes.

Return the cooked protein to the skillet. Stir gently and heat for 3-5 minutes until piping hot throughout. If too thick, add water a tablespoon at a time. Divide the cooked base and skillet mixture between two bowls and serve promptly. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and reheat until piping hot throughout.

Makes 2 servings. Use plain, unseasoned protein and vegetables. Wash produce and measure the ingredients. Cut zucchini into thin half-moons and slice the mushrooms.

Rinse the dry quinoa well. Bring it and 360 ml water to a boil in a saucepan. Cover and simmer gently for 15-20 minutes until tender. Rest off the heat for 5 minutes and fluff. Cook the skillet mixture while the base cooks.

Drain plain firm tofu, pat it dry and cut into 2 cm cubes. Heat half the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the tofu for 8-10 minutes, turning gently, until golden. Transfer to a clean plate.

Add the remaining olive oil to the skillet. Add the prepared vegetables (holding back any spinach), stir for 2 minutes, then add 60 ml water. Cover and cook over medium heat for 8-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the firmest vegetables are tender. Add any reserved spinach for the final 3 minutes. Uncover and let excess water evaporate.

Peel and finely grate the ginger. Whisk it with smooth peanut butter, lime juice, soy sauce and 90 ml warm water. Pour into the tender vegetables and simmer gently for 3 minutes, stirring.

Return the cooked protein to the skillet. Stir gently and heat for 3-5 minutes until piping hot throughout. If too thick, add water a tablespoon at a time. Divide the cooked base and skillet mixture between two bowls and serve promptly. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and reheat until piping hot throughout.

Return the cooked protein to the skillet. Stir gently and heat for 3-5 minutes until piping hot throughout. If too thick, add water a tablespoon at a time. Divide the cooked base and skillet mixture between two bowls and serve promptly. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and reheat until piping hot throughout.

Divide the cooked base and skillet mixture between two bowls and serve promptly. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and reheat until piping hot throughout.

Rinse the dry quinoa well. Bring it and 360 ml water to a boil in a saucepan. Cover and simmer gently for 15-20 minutes until tender. Rest off the heat for 5 minutes and fluff. Cook the skillet mixture while the base cooks.

Heat half the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the ground turkey, break it into small crumbles and cook for 8-12 minutes, until it reaches 165 F (74 C). Transfer to a clean plate.

Add the remaining olive oil to the skillet. Add the prepared vegetables (holding back any spinach), stir for 2 minutes, then add 60 ml water. Cover and cook over medium heat for 8-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the firmest vegetables are tender. Add any reserved spinach for the final 3 minutes. Uncover and let excess water evaporate.

Peel and finely grate the ginger; finely chop the garlic. Stir both into the tender vegetables for 1 minute. Add soy sauce, rice vinegar and 60 ml water, then simmer for 2 minutes.

Return the cooked protein to the skillet. Stir gently and heat for 3-5 minutes until piping hot throughout. If too thick, add water a tablespoon at a time. Divide the cooked base and skillet mixture between two bowls and serve promptly. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and reheat until piping hot throughout.

Makes 2 servings. Use plain, unseasoned protein and vegetables. Wash produce and measure the ingredients. Chop the tomatoes; wash and roughly chop the spinach. Reserve the spinach for the final 3 minutes of vegetable cooking.

Rinse the dry quinoa well. Bring it and 360 ml water to a boil in a saucepan. Cover and simmer gently for 15-20 minutes until tender. Rest off the heat for 5 minutes and fluff. Cook the skillet mixture while the base cooks.

Drain and rinse the canned cannellini beans. These must be canned, ready-to-eat beans, not dried beans. Heat half the olive oil in a large skillet. Stir the beans over medium heat for 5 minutes, then transfer to a plate.

Add the remaining olive oil to the skillet. Add the prepared vegetables (holding back any spinach), stir for 2 minutes, then add 60 ml water. Cover and cook over medium heat for 8-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the firmest vegetables are tender. Add any reserved spinach for the final 3 minutes. Uncover and let excess water evaporate.

Peel and finely grate the ginger; finely chop the garlic. Stir both into the tender vegetables for 1 minute. Add soy sauce, rice vinegar and 60 ml water, then simmer for 2 minutes.

Return the cooked protein to the skillet. Stir gently and heat for 3-5 minutes until piping hot throughout. If too thick, add water a tablespoon at a time. Divide the cooked base and skillet mixture between two bowls and serve promptly. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and reheat until piping hot throughout.

Rinse the dry long-grain white rice. Bring it and 320 ml water to a boil in a saucepan. Cover, reduce to low and cook for 15-20 minutes until tender and the water is absorbed. Rest covered for 5 minutes; fluff. Cook the skillet mixture while the base cooks.

Drain and rinse the canned cannellini beans. These must be canned, ready-to-eat beans, not dried beans. Heat half the olive oil in a large skillet. Stir the beans over medium heat for 5 minutes, then transfer to a plate.

Add the remaining olive oil to the skillet. Add the prepared vegetables (holding back any spinach), stir for 2 minutes, then add 60 ml water. Cover and cook over medium heat for 8-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the firmest vegetables are tender. Add any reserved spinach for the final 3 minutes. Uncover and let excess water evaporate.

Finely chop the garlic and stir it into the tender vegetables for 1 minute. Add the canned tomatoes and basil; break up the tomatoes and simmer 5 minutes.

Return the cooked protein to the skillet. Stir gently and heat for 3-5 minutes until piping hot throughout. If too thick, add water a tablespoon at a time. Divide the cooked base and skillet mixture between two bowls and serve promptly. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and reheat until piping hot throughout.
title: Tomato Basil White Bean Rice Bowl with Zucchini and Pepper
